newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei reverses losses, Taiwan futures ease.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei reverses losses, Taiwan futures ease.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures recovered most of their losses by Tuesday's close in another session characterised by sharp swings within a wide trading range.
"On Friday, there was a big drop. Yesterday there was a big recovery. Now we're going to have a tug-of-war," said a trader with a local institution.

The benchmark Nikkei 225 March contract finished 50 points lower at 18,055 after falling as low as 17,430 in earlier trade. Dealers said most participants were still bearish despite selected buying of blue-chip stocks, which spurred a partial recovery in the Nikkei share average.
"People have been taking profit on any rises but they're not taking new positions," said the trader, adding that the March Nikkei needed to climb above strong resistance at 18,750 to head higher.
"Technically, the downtrend has slowed down. But it's still not up. There's a whole battery of resistance levels above 18,000," he added.
On the downside, he said the market was supported around the 17,420-17,470 region, but a close below 17,550 would invite further declines.
The March MSCI Taiwan index contract ended at 306.7 against its opening of 310.2 on low turnover of 318 lots.
Dealers said interest was stymied by the contract's tight trading range and poor liquidity.
"It's still within a 305-311 range. There's been no change," said the trader.
Volatility in the Nikkei futures trading pit also drew interest away from Taiwan stock index futures, dealers said.
